submit your report via social media, when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 1 at 3:19PM CDT until August 7 at 1:15AM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Three Rivers.

* WHEN...Until late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...At 40.0 feet, Significant flooding reaches miles from the
main channel, flooding homes in the flood plain near Three Rivers
to Lake Corpus Christi. Up to 4 feet of water is in River Creek
Acres Subdivision, flooding several homes. Kellner Camp along
County Road 336 floods, with water several feet deep surrounding
homes. Antelope Lane is flooded cutting off access to J.I. Hailey
Subdivision at Jones River bend. Water approaches the base of homes
along the river in Buckeye Knoll Subdivision, 2 miles west of
Swinny Switch.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:15 PM CDT Saturday the stage was 39.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 20.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is currently cresting at 39.3 feet and is
expected to start falling tonight, falling into moderate flood
stage during the day Tuesday. The river is then expected to fall
below minor flood stage Thursday afternoon or Thursday night.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.headline: Dust Storm Warning issued August 1 at 5:22PM MST until August 1 at 7:15PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
The National Weather Service in Tucson has issued a

* Dust Storm Warning for...
Eastern Cochise County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 715 PM MST.

* At 522 PM MST, a large dust-storm/haboob along an strong outflow
boundary with winds gusting to 50-60 mph is currently observed
moving west to southwest through the Lordsburg Playa in New Mexico.
This dust storm will result in near zero visibility at times as it
moves into Arizona.

HAZARD...Near zero visibility.

SOURCE...Detected by National Weather Service meteorologists.

IMPACT...Dangerous life-threatening travel.

* Locations impacted include...
Douglas, Portal, Bowie, Chiricahua National Monument,
Bisbee-Douglas Airport, Pirtleville, Rucker Canyon, Paradise and
San Simon.

This includes the following highways...
Route 80 between mile markers 360 and 414. Route 181 between mile
markers 46 and 64. Route 191 between mile markers 1 and 11.
Interstate 10 between mile markers 364 and 390. Route 186 between
mile markers 351 and 359.
properties.instruction: Motorists should not drive into a dust storm. PULL ASIDE STAY ALIVE!

CMAMtext: NWS: DUST STORM WARNING til 7:15 PM MST. Be ready for a sudden drop to zero visibility.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: DUST STORM WARNING for this area until 7:15 PM MST. Be ready for sudden drop to zero visibility. Pull Aside, Stay Alive! When visibility drops, pull far off the road and put your vehicle in park. Turn the lights off and keep your foot off the brake. Infants, the elderly and those with respiratory issues urged to take precautions.
